items.stem: Which method does IFRS 3 require for accounting for a business combination?

options.rationale: Correct: IFRS 3 requires the acquisition method.
Pooling of interests is not permitted for business combinations in scope.
The equity method is for associates, not for consolidating an acquired business.
Proportionate consolidation is not the required method here.

items.explanation: Correct: IFRS 3 requires the acquisition method.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO items are generally NOT included in the cost of a business combination and are instead expensed or accounted for separately? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Acquisition-related costs such as advisory and legal fees
options.rationale: Correct: acquisition-related costs are expensed as incurred.

options.text: Costs to issue debt or equity used as consideration
options.rationale: Correct: debt and equity issue costs are accounted for under other standards, not added to goodwill.

options.text: The fair value of shares issued as consideration
options.rationale: Shares issued as consideration are part of the consideration transferred.

options.text: The fair value of cash paid to the former owners
options.rationale: Cash consideration is part of the consideration transferred.

items.explanation: Correct: acquisition-related costs are expensed as incurred.

items.stem: An acquirer measures goodwill and finds the fair value of identifiable net assets exceeds the consideration plus non-controlling interest. After reassessing the amounts, what is the required treatment of the excess?

options.text: Recognise it immediately as a gain on a bargain purchase in profit or loss
options.rationale: Correct: a confirmed excess is a bargain purchase gain recognised in profit or loss.

options.text: Defer it as a liability and release it over time
options.rationale: Negative goodwill is not deferred and released.

options.text: Add it to goodwill as a positive balance
options.rationale: An excess over cost is not positive goodwill.

options.text: Credit it directly to share capital
options.rationale: It is recognised in profit or loss, not in equity capital.

items.explanation: Correct: a confirmed excess is a bargain purchase gain recognised in profit or loss.
